_readme: Per-run monitoring log, one file per calendar day (America/Phoenix), used to generate the Daily PDF Report. Distinct from cases.json, which is the permanent case/review-queue index.
_run_note: Fourteenth scheduled run, and the first of October. 14 of 19 URLs served a catalog -- the four marketplace and social entries have no product feed and never serve one, and Flower Meadow Dream remains refused by this environment's egress proxy, as on every day since 2026-09-16. No new matches, no cases created, nothing held, nothing classified cut-roses-only. The only catalog movement was Hillside Rose Farm 146->150, and none of the four added listings carries a chart name. Every other site served exactly the same count as 2026-09-30. Your Roses held steady for a fourth day at 1,665 products with all 72 cases re-verified. HILLSIDERO-005 is absent for a third consecutive run; notably the site is adding listings again, so its continued absence is not part of a general catalog freeze. 356 of 360 cases re-verified -- the four unconfirmed are Flower Meadow Dream's 3 and that delisted listing.

sites.notes: Added to the roster on 2026-10-01 after the 06:07 scheduled run, on the user's instruction, and crawled for the first time at 11:42 MST once they had allowlisted the domain. Not part of the 06:07 pass. First Squarespace store on the roster; its catalog was read through the collection's own ?format=json view -- 154 products in a single request. The www host serves; the apex is refused by the egress proxy, which costs nothing since the crawler tries both. All 12 of its chart matches became cases BLOOMLADIE-001..012.
Facebook page; facebook.com is blocked by this environment's network egress policy at the CONNECT stage, so the page was never reached. No open product feed exists for a Facebook page in any case.
Etsy storefront; etsy.com is blocked by this environment's network egress policy at the CONNECT stage. The seller's own site (ergongzy.com) was crawled in full and carries the same catalog.

Not reached. Both www.myroseworld.com and myroseworld.com were refused by this environment's egress proxy at the CONNECT stage, so the request never reached the seller's server. This is our own network policy, not a block by the site. Unchanged since 2026-09-16. The site's 3 existing cases (MYROSEWORL-001..003) could not be re-verified and keep their 2026-09-16 Last Verified date.
Etsy shop closed (dormant). Roster entry retained per user instruction (2026-09-15); expected to stay inaccessible and not awaiting any decision.

Catalog grew back from 146 products to 150 -- the seller is adding listings again -- but HILLSIDERO-005 (Darlington, Pending) is not among them and is absent for a third consecutive run. No Darlington listing appears under any title or handle. Its Last Verified stays at 2026-09-28 and the case carries the delisting record.
Etsy storefront; etsy.com is blocked by this environment's network egress policy at the CONNECT stage.

Reached on the apex host after the www host was refused by the egress proxy. The Shopify feed returned HTTP 200 with an empty product array -- the store genuinely lists no products. Counted as checked, zero products.
Fourth clean run since recovering on 2026-09-28. Served 1,665 products again, unchanged, with all 72 of its cases re-verified present.

screenshot_limitation: Still no case has a screenshot on file -- same network-proxy limitation as prior runs (headless Chromium cannot complete a connection through this environment's egress proxy). Explained to the user in chat on 2026-09-14; awaiting their choice of approach (manual capture vs. Wayback Machine vs. environment-level fix).
_addendum_bloom_ladies: ADDED AFTER THE 06:07 RUN, at 11:42 MST, on the user's instruction: Bloom Ladies Roses (www.bloomladiesroses.com/shop), reported by the user as a possible infringer and allowlisted by them in the environment. Roster is now 18 companies / 20 URLs. It is a SQUARESPACE store, a platform the crawler could not read before today; scripts/crawl_sites.py gained a Squarespace reader (the collection's own ?format=json view) and scripts/create_cases.py a matching branch. Full catalog pulled in one request: 154 products, every one a rose, none cut-roses-only. 12 match the chart and all 12 became cases BLOOMLADIE-001..012 -- 1 Registered (BARONESSE, as 'Baronesse - cutting', $55, 5 in stock), 4 Pending (Pride of Jane, Emma Woodhouse, Darlington, Cappuccino), 1 To Be Filed, 1 Abandoned, 1 Not Applicable, 4 unstatused. Seller location is ESTIMATED and unconfirmed -- no address is published anywhere on the site, and United States / Pacific time zone comes from the site's own Squarespace configuration, which is a hosting setting rather than a stated business address. Hosting is Squarespace. The site's per-item publication and update dates were captured, a spec field no other site on the roster exposes. The 06:07 run's own crawl file is untouched; this recon is in crawl-2026-10-01-bloomladies.json. CORRECTION, same day: the first version of this run log carried the site's 12 cases but left the site itself out of the sites list, because that list was carried forward from 2026-09-30 and the new entry was never appended. The day's PDF therefore listed its findings while its Websites Checked table still showed 17 companies and never named Bloom Ladies Roses -- the user spotted it. The entry is now present with its real figures and the totals recomputed: 18 companies, 20 URLs, 15 of them serving a catalog, 9,642 product pages reviewed.
_correction_case_numbering: Two faults were found and fixed while building these cases, both before anything was pushed or published. (1) The site code came out as 'WWW': create_cases.py derived the domain from the roster URL without stripping the host's www prefix or the /shop path, then took everything before the first dot. It now strips both and takes everything before the final dot, giving BLOOMLADIE. Checked against every site already on the roster -- KATEROSES, YOURROSES, MOLAROSE, HIGHGARDEN, HUNIUROSEG and the rest all compute identically, so no existing case number is affected, and stored codes are reused rather than recomputed in any case. (2) Every price read $0.00, because on this platform the item-level price is a placeholder and the real price sits on the variant; a zero is now treated as no price rather than recorded as a real one. The twelve cases were deleted and rebuilt after each fix, so BLOOMLADIE-001..012 are the first and only numbers these listings have carried.
